rfp_requirements.title: Provide special replacement sticker area within CIF
rfp_requirements.description: The Contractor shall provide a special area within the CIF locations for issuing replacement stickers, including new car dealer stickers for vehicles designated under N.J.S.A. 39:8-2.

rfp_requirements.title: Award contracts in accordance with P.L.1954, c.48
rfp_requirements.description: Any contract awarded under this section must be awarded in accordance with the provisions of P.L.1954, c.48 (C.52:34-6 et seq.) and its rules and regulations.

rfp_requirements.title: Standardize qualification questionnaire in invitation to bid
rfp_requirements.description: Any required questionnaire must be standardized and set forth in each invitation to bid.

rfp_requirements.title: Prohibition on State officers/employees involved in award from bidding
rfp_requirements.description: A State officer or employee with duties or responsibilities in connection with the evaluation or awarding of a contract under this section must not, individually or through any person/entity acting on their behalf, bid on or enter into a contract as a private contractor.

rfp_requirements.title: Conduct periodic surveys concerning hours and methods of operation
rfp_requirements.description: Periodic surveys concerning hours and methods of operation must be conducted.

rfp_requirements.title: Include EPA Administrator and NJ Congressional member contact info in written document
rfp_requirements.description: The written document provided to motorists must include the name and address of the Administrator of the United States Environmental Protection Agency and of each member of Congress elected from this State.

rfp_requirements.title: Offer full-time employment to qualified terminated MVC full-time employees
rfp_requirements.description: All qualified full-time employees whose employment with the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission is terminated as a result of P.L.1995, c.112 must be offered full-time employment by the contractor(s).

rfp_requirements.title: Chief Administrator may issue directives/guidelines or enter oversight contracts
rfp_requirements.description: The chief administrator may issue directives or guidelines or enter into contracts or agreements for the oversight and regulation of any person who has entered into a contract with the State pursuant to subsection a.

rfp_requirements.title: State Treasurer may consent to early filing notwithstanding N.J.S.59:13-5
rfp_requirements.description: Any provision of N.J.S.59:13-5 to the contrary notwithstanding, the State Treasurer may consent to the filing of a dispute request prior to the expiration of 90 days from the date that the notice of claim is received.

rfp_requirements.title: Court authority to order ADR (dispute resolution, mediation, arbitration)
rfp_requirements.description: The court may take such action as it deems necessary to facilitate expeditious resolution, including ordering the parties to undertake dispute resolution, mediation, or arbitration as provided in N.J.S.59:13-7.

rfp_requirements.title: Employment offers must include compensation and economic benefits comparable to existing CBA

B.5 Overt Oversight Activities
We successfully deliver a completely neutral, unbiased QA program that meets the requirements of 40 CFR § 51.363
(a) (1) through (3) and 51.363 (b) through (d) and other applicable federal regulations as they apply to PA I/M Program.
To date, Parsons has conducted more than 372,000 overt audits in the PA I/M Program. We are not involved with any
I/M equipment provider in Pennsylvania, supporting our impartial approach to all aspects of the oversight process.
This experience will allow our team to complete emission station and equipment audit operations more effectively
than any other team.
The overt audit provides a visible presence for PennDOT in I/M inspection stations and allows for education and
enforcement of Program regulations. All overt audits are scheduled on the following criteria: date of last audit, record
audit data analysis, consumer complaints, covert audit results, and/or PennDOT requests. Parsons will complete two
unannounced overt audits during normal business hours per year for each I/M station, regardless of location in the
Commonwealth. The audit will include an examination o

o PennDOT’s regulations. We will verify that I/M inspections at each station are
performed by certified I/M inspectors, that certified repair technicians deliver waivers, and that I/M inspections are
recorded as required by PennDOT regulations in the PennDOT Vehicle Inspection System. Parsons’ team will minimize
disruption to station operations during these visits.

experience conducting audits.

B.7 Remote Visual Observation of Inspectors
We will perform remote visual audits using our covert audit staff and infrastructure to ensure station compliance with
the rules and regulations of the I/M Program. Our team will perform remote visual audits targeted at those stations
performing more than 4,000 inspections per year as per 40 CFR § 51.363 (a) (4). We also have the capacity to conduct
remote visual audits if we find discrepancies at stations through other auditing functions or consumer complaints.
Our auditors will use nondescript vehicles to view station activities from a safe distance. We will also have the ability to
use field glasses, record video, or take still pictures of activities performed at an inspection station, at PennDOT’s
direction. While the auditor is observing, they will record notes (including license plate and vehicle make/model/color)
on the remote visual audit application. The audit application will enable photographs to be appended to the audit
record as well. As in the case of any I/M violation, the audit manager will submit a report documenting the findi

all covert audit reports for accuracy and completeness, including attached pictures and
documentation, and then forward them to PennDOT’s Vehicle Inspection System. The covert audit manager will flag
violations for PennDOT, as per their guidelines, for appropriate action against I/M inspection stations, I/M inspectors,
or other persons violating state law or PennDOT regulations. Parsons developed the current covert audit report with
guidance and approval from PennDOT. We will supply copies of updated operations manuals and report formats for
PennDOT approval.

compromised in a location. We will rotate vehicles out of the fleet after use in all areas. Parsons has made provisions to
maintain an adequate covert fleet of vehicles representative of the subject vehicles in terms of vehicle type and age.

A cornerstone of the PA I/M Program is ensuring inspection equipment and software conforms to the required

equipment in the I/M Program, with no financial interest in any EM, will ensure integrity in the acceptance testing

ATPs
Our PennDOT-approved testing procedures ensure that all applicable specifications, calibrations, quality control
requirements, and other requirements contained in EPA rules and PA I/M regulations are met by all equipment offered
for use in the PA I/M Program. We also include processes to ensure the software meets all I/M Program requirements.
We developed comprehensive ATP scripts for every equipment implementation and update in the PA I/M Program.
Coordination with EMs
In addition to the testing procedures, Parsons developed a PennDOT-approved set of procedures for coordinating
certification efforts with EMs. We will ensure the EMs have the information they require to install the data transmission
software in their equipment in a timely fashion. We provide all participating EMs with ATPs for their own internal testing
